key_insight: A new theoretical analysis shows that the randomized Hadamard transform (HD) can be used with scalar quantization to get provable compression/error guarantees similar to dense random rotations, while reducing computation from Θ(d^2) to O(d log d). This bridges the gap between fast structured transforms and rigorous quantization guarantees.
problem_solved: Removes the lack of provable error bounds for quantization schemes based on the discrete randomized Hadamard transform, enabling fast (near-linear) projection-plus-quantization with theoretical guarantees previously available only for dense random rotations.
method: Replace dense random rotations with the randomized Hadamard transform HD to obtain O(d log d) preprocessing.
Develop novel probabilistic/analytic bounds for HD’s discrete structure to prove end-to-end quantization error guarantees after scalar quantization.
Validate theory with experiments on representative ML tasks (e.g., similarity search, federated learning, KV cache compression) to show practical accuracy/runtime trade-offs.
impact: Provides a practical, provably-correct recipe for high-throughput vector quantization in large-scale ML systems, enabling faster compression and inference without sacrificing theoretical guarantees. This makes structured, low-cost transforms a trustworthy choice for production pipelines.
